artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

Let $p$ be a prime and let $g$ be a primitive root modulo $p$. The exponential Welch Costas permutation $f_g$ on $\{0,1,\dots,p-2\}$ is defined by $f_g(i) = g^i \bmod p - 1$. Two Welch permutations $f_{g_1}$ and $f_{g_2}$ are said to be produced by different primitive roots, written $f_{g_1} \stackrel{pr}{\neq} f_{g_2}$, if $g_1 \not\equiv g_2 \pmod p$.

Let $q$ be a prime power and let $\alpha,\beta$ be primitive elements of the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. The Golomb Costas permutation $f'_{\alpha,\beta}$ on $\{1,\dots,q-2\}$ is defined by the relation $\alpha^{i} + \beta^{f'_{\alpha,\beta}(i)} = 1$.

For two permutations $f_1, f_2$ of a common index set of size $N$ and integers $(u,v)$ with $|u|<N$, define the cross-correlation
$$\Psi_{f_1,f_2}(u,v) = \#\{ i : f_1(i+u) = f_2(i) + v \}.$$

Define
$$\Psi_{W_1}(p) = \max_{(u,v)} \max_{f_1 \stackrel{pr}{\neq} f_2} \Psi_{f_1,f_2}(u,v),$$
$$\Psi_{G_2}(q) = \max_{(u,v)} \max_{f'_1 \neq f'_2} \Psi_{f'_1,f'_2}(u,v),$$
the maxima being taken over pairs of distinct Welch (resp. Golomb) Costas permutations as above.

A prime $p$ is called safe if $(p-1)/2$ is also prime.

Problem.

(a) Prove that with respect to $\Psi_{W_1}(p)$ and $\Psi_{G_2}(p)$, the primes $p$ split into three groups according to whether $p$ is a safe prime, $p$ is a non-safe prime of a specified second class, or $p$ is a non-safe prime of the third class, and determine the corresponding closed-form values (or sharp bounds) of $\Psi_{W_1}(p)$ and $\Psi_{G_2}(p)$ in each class, including all exceptional small cases.

(b) Prove the analogous trichotomy classification of prime powers $q$ with respect to $\Psi_{G_2}(q)$, with the corresponding formulas and exceptional cases.

(c) For non-safe primes $p$, prove that
$$\Psi_{W_1}(p) = \max_{f_1 \stackrel{pr}{\neq} f_2} \Psi_{f_1,f_2}(0,0),$$
i.e. the maximum is attained at the shift $(u,v)=(0,0)$. For prime powers $q \notin \{16,19\}$ that are non-safe and such that $q-1$ is not prime, prove that
$$\Psi_{G_2}(q) = \max_{f'_1 \neq f'_2} \Psi_{f'_1,f'_2}(0,0).$$

(d) Derive explicit formulas for the local minima of $\Psi_{W_1}$ and $\Psi_{G_2}$ in terms of arithmetic invariants of $p$ and $q$ (e.g. the smallest prime divisor of $p-1$ or $q-1$).
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work (notably the 2020 IEEE Transactions on Information Theory note "A Note on the Cross-Correlation of Costas Permutations") settles part of the conjecture: for primes $p\ge 5$, the maximal cross-correlation of distinct Welch Costas permutations equals $(p-1)/t$ where $t$ is the smallest prime divisor of $(p-1)/2$ when $p$ is not safe, and is at most $1+\sqrt{p}$ when $p$ is safe. The corresponding Golomb result is proved only for a smaller subfamily of size $\varphi(q-1)$, and the authors note the bound can fail for the full Golomb family of size $\varphi(q-1)^2$. Hence the trichotomy classification and formulas are partially proved, with the full Golomb case and several exceptional/local-minimum statements still open.

status_evidence.title: A Note on the Cross-Correlation of Costas Permutations
status_evidence.snippet: For a prime p≥5, the maximal cross-correlation of the family of different Welch Costas permutations is (p-1)/t, where t is the smallest prime divisor of (p-1)/2 if p is not a safe prime and at most 1+p^(1/2) otherwise.
status_evidence.claim: Settles the Welch part of the conjecture and a subfamily Golomb case; full Golomb case remains open.

status_evidence.title: On the cross-correlation properties of large-size families of Costas arrays
status_evidence.snippet: Studies maximal cross-correlation over Welch and Golomb families with conjectures and partial proofs.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates ongoing work on the same family of conjectures, with several still unresolved.
